task_prompts.go-flag--url:
Add a new flag type to urfave/cli: `cli.URLFlag`, which accepts an absolute URL (it must have a scheme and a host) and parses it into a `*url.URL`. Its value is read with a new accessor `cmd.URL(name string) *url.URL`. A value it cannot parse must make the command fail with an error. Examples of valid input: `https://example.com/x`, `http://localhost:8080`. Examples of invalid input: `example.com`, `not a url`, `://x`.

Include tests, list the new flag in the flags documentation, and update the generated API documentation, as the project does for new flag types.
task_prompts.go-flag--port:
Add a new flag type to urfave/cli: `cli.PortFlag`, which accepts a TCP/UDP port number, an integer from 1 to 65535 inclusive, as a `uint16`. Its value is read with a new accessor `cmd.Port(name string) uint16`. A value it cannot parse must make the command fail with an error. Examples of valid input: `80`, `65535`, `1`. Examples of invalid input: `0`, `70000`, `http`.

Include tests, list the new flag in the flags documentation, and update the generated API documentation, as the project does for new flag types.
task_prompts.go-flag--regexp:
Add a new flag type to urfave/cli: `cli.RegexpFlag`, which accepts a regular expression and compiles it into a `*regexp.Regexp`. Its value is read with a new accessor `cmd.Regexp(name string) *regexp.Regexp`. A value it cannot parse must make the command fail with an error. Examples of valid input: `^a+$`, `[0-9]{3}`. Examples of invalid input: `(`, `a[`.

Include tests, list the new flag in the flags documentation, and update the generated API documentation, as the project does for new flag types.
task_prompts.go-flag--ip:
Add a new flag type to urfave/cli: `cli.IPFlag`, which accepts an IPv4 or IPv6 address and parses it into a `net.IP`. Its value is read with a new accessor `cmd.IP(name string) net.IP`. A value it cannot parse must make the command fail with an error. Examples of valid input: `127.0.0.1`, `::1`. Examples of invalid input: `999.1.1.1`, `localhost`.

Include tests, list the new flag in the flags documentation, and update the generated API documentation, as the project does for new flag types.
task_prompts.go-flag--percent:
Add a new flag type to urfave/cli: `cli.PercentFlag`, which accepts a percentage from 0 to 100 inclusive, written with or without a trailing `%` (for example `50%`, `12.5`), as a `float64` fraction (`50%` is `0.5`). Its value is read with a new accessor `cmd.Percent(name string) float64`. A value it cannot parse must make the command fail with an error. Examples of valid input: `50%`, `12.5`, `100%`. Examples of invalid input: `101%`, `-1`, `abc`.

Include tests, list the new flag in the flags documentation, and update the generated API documentation, as the project does for new flag types.
task_prompts.go-flag--bytesize:
Add a new flag type to urfave/cli: `cli.ByteSizeFlag`, which accepts a size in bytes written as a number with an optional unit: `B`, `KB`, `MB`, `GB` (powers of 1000) or `KiB`, `MiB`, `GiB` (powers of 1024), case-insensitive, as an `int64` number of bytes (a bare number is bytes; `1.5MB` is `1500000`). Its value is read with a new accessor `cmd.ByteSize(name string) int64`. A value it cannot parse must make the command fail with an error. Examples of valid input: `10KB`, `1KiB`, `512`, `1.5MB`. Examples of invalid input: `10XB`, `-1KB`, `KB`.

task_prompts.go-flag--date:

Examples of invalid input: `2024-13-01`, `01/02/2024`, `2023-02-29`.

task_prompts.go-flag--hexcolor:
Add a new flag type to urfave/cli: `cli.HexColorFlag`, which accepts a CSS hex color written as `#RGB` or `#RRGGBB` (case-insensitive, the `#` is required) and normalizes it to the lower-case 6-digit form `#rrggbb` (a `string`). Its value is read with a new accessor `cmd.HexColor(name string) string`. A value it cannot parse must make the command fail with an error. Examples of valid input: `#FFF`, `#1a2B3c`. Examples of invalid input: `fff`, `#12345`, `#ggg`.

task_prompts.go-flag--hostport:
Add a new flag type to urfave/cli: `cli.HostPortFlag`, which accepts a `host:port` pair (a non-empty host, IPv6 hosts in brackets, and a port from 1 to 65535) and keeps it as a `string`. Its value is read with a new accessor `cmd.HostPort(name string) string`. A value it cannot parse must make the command fail with an error. Examples of valid input: `localhost:8080`, `[::1]:443`. Examples of invalid input: `localhost`, `:80`, `host:0`, `host:http`.

task_prompts.go-flag--uuid:
Add a new flag type to urfave/cli: `cli.UUIDFlag`, which accepts a UUID in its canonical 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal form (case-insensitive) and normalizes it to lower case (a `string`). Examples of invalid input: `123e4567e89b12d3a456426614174000`, `not-a-uuid`, `123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-42661417400g`.
